tierWindow.goal: Understand what it means to excel at university, and recognise the mindset, self-belief and motivation that a successful student brings from the start.
tierWindow.cognitiveDemand: Recognition, recall, description and guided identification (understand and identify).
tierWindow.taskComplexity: Well-defined, one idea at a time; settled distinctions such as growth versus fixed mindset and learning versus performance motivation.
tierWindow.autonomy: High scaffolding; worked examples; feedback confirms and explains; frequent low-stakes checks.

decidedValue.priorExperienceAnchor: No prior experience of thinking about mindset, motivation or what success really means at university is assumed. The learner is just starting their studies and may equate success only with high marks; teach from first principles.

decidedValue.signpostBody: The course has three short lessons. First, what it means to excel: success as more than marks. Second, a growth mindset: how believing you can improve, and trusting you can succeed, support your studies. Third, understanding your motivation: the difference between studying to perform and studying to learn. Work through them in order; each builds on the one before.
decidedValue.signpostInstruction: Work through the three lessons in order.
decidedValue.overview:
This short course is about starting well at university: what it really means to excel, and the mindset and motivation that successful students bring from the start. By the end you will be able to explain what excelling means, describe how a growth mindset and self-efficacy support success, and tell learning motivation apart from performance motivation.

These are not abstract ideas. How you think about your own ability, and what drives you to study, shape the effort you put in and how you respond when work gets hard. Getting this right at the start changes how the rest of your degree feels.
decidedValue.courseOutcomesFraming: Three course outcomes framed up front: explain what excelling means, describe how a growth mindset and self-efficacy support success, and distinguish learning from performance motivation.

practiceConnection.academic: Starting well is the foundation the rest of your degree is built on. The mindset you bring to your first assignments, the belief that you can improve with effort, and the reasons you study all shape how you work in every module that follows. Build these now and they carry through your studies, and into the working life your degree leads to.

grounding.note: wrapper grounded in the three course outcomes (AL-5)

decidedValue.whereNextBody: Two directions build on this. Going deeper: the intermediate and advanced Starting, Progressing and Succeeding courses take these foundations into setting and regulating your own goals, and into building the graduate capital that employers value. Going wider: the same foundations underpin Reflective Practice, Academic Writing and Researching, where you put the mindset to work on real tasks.
decidedValue.summary: You have reached the end of the course. Excelling is no longer just about marks: it is something you can describe and begin to aim for. You can explain what excelling means, success as both academic performance and personal development, approached as a mindset rather than a fixed trait. You can describe how a growth mindset and self-efficacy support success. And you can tell learning motivation apart from performance motivation. Look back at the confidence check: comparing where you started with where you are now shows how far this has moved.

practiceConnection.academic: From here, starting well is something you practise in every module. Each assignment you approach as a chance to grow and not only to score, each setback you meet with effort rather than retreat, each time you study to understand rather than only to perform, is this mindset at work. It is also what working life rewards: people who keep learning, believe they can improve, and know what drives them go further.

courseReferences.title: See pages 9 to 26 of Chapter 2, 'Excelling at university: Mindset, motivation, and goals', of Excelling at University by Dennis and Abbott (2026).
